result:
I can't write that message as asked, because the evidence doesn't support "the new button wins." Two problems:

- **Daily peeking:** Checking a fixed-horizon test every day for 3 weeks and stopping on the first p<0.05 inflates the false-positive rate well above 5%. Without a sequential-testing correction, p=0.04 is weak.
- **12 metrics:** If the purchases-per-visitor metric wasn't pre-registered as the primary one, the chance that at least one of 12 hits p<0.05 is around 46% under no true effect. A +1.1% relative lift that appeared after 20 flat days looks like noise.

Here is a two-line message that reflects what the data shows:

> Checkout button test: no reliable win yet. Purchases/visitor reached p=0.04 (+1.1% relative) only on the last day, after daily peeking and 12 tracked metrics, so it doesn't survive correction.
> Recommend we extend to the pre-planned sample size (or rerun with purchases/visitor as the sole primary metric), and ship only if it holds. If the button is cheap and reversible, shipping with a holdback is a reasonable alternative.

If the metric was pre-registered as primary and you had a fixed stopping rule, tell me and I'll rewrite it more favorably. If you want a quick check, I can also compute the corrected threshold if you share the planned sample size and the number of looks.
